title: Menu items that are settings wear a checkmark instead of rewording themselves
goal: Show Grid changes its wording to Hide Grid when the grid is on, and Snap to Grid becomes Stop Snapping to Grid. That is how an action is written, not a setting. Every menu item that is simply on or off should keep one name and carry a checkmark when it is on, so you can see the state without reading a sentence, and so the item does not move under the pointer as its label changes length. That goes for all of them, panels and the history included, not just the grid.
notes: Asked for by the user on 2026-09-05, then confirmed for ALL stateful items rather than just the grid, so no per item judgement is needed: convert every one. No menu item in the app uses a checkmark today. EditorCommands.swift flips titles at line 527 (grid), 536 (snapping), 492 (layers panel) and 503 (Library), and MainMenuTitles.swift retitles the history item from a separate file. That history item is reached from the menu bar agent as well as the editor and there is an open task about the two disagreeing (show-history-and-hide-history-agree-with-whether); read it first and make sure this change resolves rather than deepens it. SwiftUI menu items take a Toggle for exactly this, which also reports the right state to accessibility, rather than drawing a tick by hand. Leave true actions alone, for example Play and Pause at line 183 and Crop to Region at 198.
acceptance: Every menu item that holds an on or off state keeps a single name and carries a checkmark when it is on: the grid, snapping, the layers panel, the Library and the history, plus any other found while doing it
No menu item is left flipping its wording to say what state it is in; the audit lists every item changed and confirms none were missed
An item that genuinely performs an action, such as playing or pausing, is left alone, and the audit says which those are
Each one still works from its keyboard shortcut, and the shortcut is shown once rather than moving between two items
The history item reads the same in the menu bar agent and in the editor window, since it is retitled from a second place
Nothing changes about what any of them does
Audit written under queue/audits/ with the View menu and the history item in both states, anything rough filed as a follow-up
